skill.name: verging-ai-tts
skill.description: Convert text to speech audio using OpenAI TTS-1-HD through the verging.ai proxy API. Supports multiple voices, playback speed control, and various audio output formats.
skill.summary: Generate spoken audio from text through the verging.ai TTS API.
skill.author: verging-ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for a verging.ai text-to-speech API workflow. Confirmed risks are limited to intentional outbound requests that send text to verging.ai and receive CDN audio URLs. Placeholder API key examples, Markdown code fences, and the error-code table are false positives.

remediation.issue: Outbound text is sent to a third-party TTS service.
remediation.suggestion: State clearly that input text goes to verging.ai and may be processed by an upstream TTS provider.

remediation.issue: API key examples appear in setup and request documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Keep using placeholders and add guidance to avoid pasting real keys into prompts, logs, or shared files.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast spoken audio for scripts, demos, and product content. This skill shows how Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can call verging.ai TTS and return audio links.
actual_capabilities: Sends text to the verging.ai TTS endpoint for speech generation.
Uses OpenAI TTS-1-HD through the verging.ai proxy API.
Supports alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, and shimmer voices.
Documents playback speed control from 0.25x to 4.0x.
Returns a generated audio URL and credits consumed.
limitations: Requires a verging.ai API key and available account credits.
Sends input text to an external service for processing.
Limits each input request to 4096 characters.
Depends on API availability, rate limits, and upstream provider status.

use_cases.title: Create Short Narration
use_cases.description: Turn a marketing script or product note into a downloadable spoken MP3.

use_cases.title: Prototype Voice Features
use_cases.description: Test voice choices and speed settings before adding TTS to an application.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accessible Audio
use_cases.description: Generate audio versions of brief help text, onboarding copy, or release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Basic Speech
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single audio file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tts skill to convert this text into MP3 speech with the nova voice at normal speed: [text].

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Voice
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a voice before generating audio.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the supported voices for this script. Recommend one voice, then generate speech with that voice: [script].

prompt_templates.title: Create Multiple Takes
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate three versions of this announcement using alloy, nova, and onyx. Use speeds 0.9, 1.0, and 1.1: [announcement].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Narrated Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for longer product copy.
prompt_templates.prompt: Split this walkthrough into sections under 4096 characters. Select a voice for each section, generate audio, and summarize URLs, voices, speeds, and credits.

output_examples.input: Generate a nova voice greeting for a new user onboarding screen.
output_examples.output: Audio created with nova at normal speed. The result includes a CDN MP3 link and the credits consumed.

output_examples.input: Create three versions of a product update with different voices.
output: Alloy version created for a neutral tone.
Nova version created for a brighter tone.
Onyx version created for a deeper tone.

output_examples.input: Turn a long help article into narrated sections.
output_examples.output: The article is split into request-sized sections. Each section receives a voice, speed, audio link, and credit count.

best_practices: Split long scripts before they exceed the 4096 character limit.
Store API keys in environment variables and keep them out of shared prompts.
Review generated audio before publishing it to users or customers.
anti_patterns: Do not submit passwords, secrets, or private customer data for speech generation.
Do not paste real API keys into chat messages or shared documentation.
Do not assume the remote API is always available or free of rate limits.

faq.question: Does this skill require a verging.ai account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need a verging.ai API key and account credits before making requests.

faq.question: Which voices are supported?
faq.answer: The documented voices are alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, and shimmer.

faq.question: What model does it use?
faq.answer: The skill documents OpenAI TTS-1-HD through the verging.ai proxy API.

faq.question: Is my text sent outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The request sends input text to verging.ai for speech generation.

faq.question: Can I change the playback speed?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented speed range is 0.25x to 4.0x.

faq.question: What happens when credits or rate limits are exhausted?
faq.answer: The API may return errors for insufficient credits, rate limits, upstream failures, or service unavailability.
